page_title: Carbon: meeting transcripts that stay on your Mac

sources.entry: Carbon - Menu bar app that transcribes meetings on device and saves each one as a Markdown file, with no bot and no cloud. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/AlexDemzz/carbon) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Carbon
summary.one_liner: Carbon is a free, MIT-licensed native macOS menu bar app that transcribes meetings on-device and saves each one as a Markdown file, without joining the call as a bot.
use_cases: Transcribing Zoom, Teams, Webex, Google Meet or FaceTime calls on a Mac
Creating searchable meeting notes for an AI agent to read
Keeping meeting transcripts private on a local machine
Recording who said what in a call with speaker labels
Building a local archive of meeting transcripts as Markdown files
summary.what_it_does: Carbon runs in the macOS menu bar and starts transcribing when a meeting app such as Zoom, Google Meet, Teams or another app begins using the microphone. It transcribes with Apple's on-device speech recognition (SpeechTranscriber) and deletes the audio once the transcript is written, unless Keep audio after transcribing is enabled. It labels your voice as "Me" and other voices as Speaker A, B and C, uses calendar events for meeting titles and participants, and lets you name voices so it recognizes them later. Each meeting is saved as a plain Markdown file with front matter (provider, date, title, duration, participants) and one line per speaker turn with a timestamp; the shortcut Shift+Command+C copies the file path for use with an AI agent. Users can edit transcripts without Carbon overwriting their changes.
notable: Joins no call and adds no bot; runs locally with no account, analytics or server
Saves each meeting as a Markdown file with speaker names and timestamps for AI agents such as Claude Code and Codex
Uses Apple's on-device speech recognition and deletes audio after transcription by default
MIT licensed with source code on GitHub
caveats: Requires macOS 26 or later on Apple silicon
Needs microphone, system audio recording and calendar access permissions
Recording others without consent is left to the user's responsibility
